findings.title: Bullet margin rule removed from extra-info badge wrapper without replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule nested under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`. Nothing replaces it, so bullet-style category badges in the extra-info area lose their 5px top offset and the vertical alignment they relied on. The PR's stated goal is performance, and this is an unrelated visual regression.

findings.title: Float rules on children of the new flex container are ignored
findings.body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container (line 264-265), but its children still rely on floats: `.topic-avatar { float: left }` (line 270), `.avatar { float: left }` and the `button { float: right }` at line 309. Floated flex items are ignored, so the avatar and action buttons will be positioned differently than before. Those floats need to be replaced with flex properties or the layout needs to be verified.

findings.title: Unrelated spacing changes to .small-action-desc alter the layout
findings.body: The padding of `.small-action-desc` changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` plus `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%` (line 280). The left indent of 4em is removed, along with the `padding-top: 4px` on `> p` and the `margin: 5px 0` on `.custom-message p`. These are visual changes that a flexbox conversion does not require, and the PR does not explain them. They will shift the text and avatar alignment in small action rows.

findings.title: Removal of the .title float rule and .panel float may break header markup
findings.body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule is deleted from `.d-header .contents`, and `.panel` switches from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` with `order(3)` (lines 17-19 and 36-41). These only work if every affected child is a direct flex item of `.contents`. Any `.title` element nested deeper, or any child that is not a flex item, will lose its float with no replacement. Nothing in the PR shows this was checked.

findings.title: Flexbox mixins added without checking for existing definitions
findings.body: New `flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items` and `order` mixins are appended to the shared foundation file. If equivalent mixins already exist elsewhere in the stylesheets, Sass will silently use the later definition, and the mixin's vendor prefixes or argument handling can change every existing `@include` site. The PR does not show that the names are unique. Also, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property and should be removed.
